extracted.intended_audience: Citizens and delegates considering ratification of the proposed U.S. Constitution; political readers evaluating the scope and prudence of federal powers
extracted.subtask_description: Analytic/persuasive evaluation of the powers conferred by the proposed U.S. Constitution, discussing which powers are necessary, how they should be limited, and how they compare to prior practice under the Confederation and foreign examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of a power for the public good
rubrics_metrics.description: “The point first to be decided is, whether such a power be necessary to the public good.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate any contemplated federal power by asking whether it is a necessary means to a necessary end; accept that all political institutions involve tradeoffs and that the choice is among greater or lesser goods rather than perfect solutions. Consider whether the power materially advances public happiness before conferring it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarding against perversion of conferred powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Powers granted should be accompanied by effective safeguards “to guard as effectually as possible against a perversion of the power to the public detriment.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When approving broad powers, also design limitations, terms, enumerations, and institutional checks to reduce risk of abuse. Examine structural features (e.g., terms of appropriation, election frequency) that constrain misuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess aggregate federal power: necessary vs dangerous
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask (1) whether any transferred powers are unnecessary or improper, and (2) whether the whole mass of transferred powers is dangerous to state jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance the aggregate scope of federal authority against retained state powers; determine if individual powers are justified as means to essential ends and whether the total allocation imperils state sovereignty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review powers by classified objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce the powers into classes to review them conveniently: (1) security against foreign danger; (2) regulation of intercourse with foreign nations; (3) maintenance of harmony and proper intercourse among the States; (4) miscellaneous objects of general utility; (5) restraint of the States from certain injurious acts; (6) provisions for giving due efficacy to all these powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a taxonomy of objectives to judge each power in context and to see whether the Constitution provides both substantive authorities and limits appropriate to each class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security against foreign danger: necessary defensive powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Powers requisite for national defense: declaring war, granting letters of marque, providing armies and fleets, regulating and calling forth the militia, and levying and borrowing money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept broad defensive powers as necessary to self-preservation; consider that limiting defensive capacity artificially (e.g., forbidding peace establishments) would be imprudent because means of security must be tailored to the means and danger of attack.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing armies: recognize danger but permit necessary readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: A standing force is dangerous though it may be necessary; prudence requires diminishing both the necessity and the danger of resorting to standing armies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide institutional features (union, terms for appropriation, civilian control) to reduce need for large standing forces and to check their dangers. Emphasize measures that minimize the probability and consequences of peace-time standing establishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on army appropriations (two-year term) as a safeguard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Constitution limits the term for which revenue may be appropriated to army support to two years; this is a prudential constraint compared to no formal British limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the sufficiency of appropriation-term limits in light of representative accountability (elections every second year) and practical restraints on legislative discretion; compare actual practice (e.g., annual British votes) rather than formal text alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union reduces need for dangerous military establishments
rubrics_metrics.description: A united America will not require the same large peace establishments as disunited states; the Union itself diminishes pretexts for dangerous military establishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate defense-related powers with the premise that a stable Union mitigates security threats and thus reduces the scale of military establishments that would be necessary under disunion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navy provision as a principal and safe source of security
rubrics_metrics.description: The power to provide and maintain a navy is a principal source of security against foreign danger and is among the greatest blessings of the Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat naval powers as especially appropriate because naval defenses are less likely to be turned inward against liberties; weigh maritime needs (coastal states’ vulnerability) when judging necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation and revenue powers must accommodate economic change
rubrics_metrics.description: Revenue from foreign commerce will vary with imports and economic development; a long-lived government must contemplate such revolutions and not be restricted to external taxation only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject arguments that federal taxation should be limited to exports/imports; consider shifting economic bases (domestic manufactures, raw-material exports) and ensure revenue powers can adapt over time to meet public needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construe the 'general welfare' clause in light of enumerated powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The clause empowering Congress 'to lay and collect taxes...to provide for the common defence and general welfare' is not an unlimited commission to legislate on all matters — the enumerated powers that follow explain and qualify it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret broad language together with subsequent specific enumerations; do not read the general welfare phrase as freeing Congress to legislate in all cases absent the enumerated authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate proposals by merit rather than origin
rubrics_metrics.description: The prudent inquiry should be 'not so much from whom the advice comes, as whether the advice be good.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging a proposed constitution or reform, focus on substantive utility and capacity to promote public happiness rather than on procedural or source-based objections; accept useful propositions even if originating in irregular ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers regulating intercourse with foreign nations
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal powers include making treaties; sending and receiving ambassadors, other public ministers, and consuls; defining and punishing piracies and felonies on the high seas; regulating foreign commerce, including the postponed power to prohibit importation of slaves after 1808 and an intermediate duty of ten dollars per head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat foreign-affairs powers as essential for one nation to act coherently abroad; note that the Constitution improves on Confederation defects (e.g., states obstructing treaties) and provides for necessary grades of public ministers and consuls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative definition needed for felonies on the high seas
rubrics_metrics.description: A definition of felonies on the high seas is 'evidently requisite' because the term is of loose signification and varies across states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor a federal legislative definition for uniformity and certainty rather than relying on disparate state statutes or the variable law of nations; uniform criminal definitions prevent embroiling the Union with foreign nations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interstate commerce regulation to preserve harmony among States
rubrics_metrics.description: Powers to regulate commerce among the several States and with Indian tribes (and related powers) are essential to prevent states from imposing tolls, duties, or regulations that would burden neighboring states and produce animosities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess interstate-commerce authority by its capacity to prevent retaliatory or predatory state measures, to secure free passage of goods, and to avoid fracturing national tranquility and prosperity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miscellaneous federal powers for uniformity and efficacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal powers include: coin money and regulate its value; punish counterfeiting; fix weights and measures; establish a uniform rule of naturalization; uniform laws of bankruptcy; prescribe how public acts/records/judicial proceedings are proved and affect other states; establish post offices and post roads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these miscellaneous powers as necessary tools to secure economic and legal uniformity across the Union; their practical absence under the Confederation produced concrete mischiefs.
